title: Initial kinetic energy
description: Essential Criteria: The response must state that the initial kinetic energy equals eU, derived from the work-energy theorem for acceleration across voltage U.

title: Maximum kinetic energy
description: Essential Criteria: The response must give the final expression for maximum kinetic energy as e²B²R²/(2m), derived from combining circular motion force balance with kinetic energy formula.

title: AC frequency expression
description: Essential Criteria: The response must state the AC frequency as eB/(2πm), derived from matching the proton's cyclotron period to the supply period.

title: Circular motion force balance
description: Important Criteria: The solution must apply Newton's second law for circular motion (evB = mv²/R) to relate velocity, magnetic field, and radius.

title: Period-frequency relationship
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly relate frequency and period (f = 1/T) and identify the cyclotron period as T = 2πm/(eB).

title: Work-energy theorem application
description: Important Criteria: The solution must apply the work-energy theorem (eU = ΔE_k) to find the initial kinetic energy from the accelerating voltage.

title: Confusing initial and final energy
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly equates the initial kinetic energy (eU) with the maximum kinetic energy (e²B²R²/(2m)).

title: Incorrect period or frequency formula
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student uses an incorrect formula for the cyclotron period (e.g., T = 2πR/v instead of T = 2πm/(eB)) or misrelates frequency and period.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional Criteria: The solution may include verification that all derived expressions have correct physical units (energy in joules, frequency in hertz).
